page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g-120s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core and 2 threads, powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and a bundled 120 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. No GPU accelerators are included. The instance also comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression tests scoring in the top 10% tier. Geekbench single-core and text processing benchmarks also demonstrate strong performance in the top 25% tier. However, multi-core and parallel processing workloads show limitations, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation tests falling into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is average for large blocks but weak for small cached blocks.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a stable resource profile for workloads that rely heavily on single-threaded execution. It is well-suited for lightweight static web serving, single-threaded text processing, and basic utility tasks. However, it is less efficient for highly parallelized applications, database operations, or large-scale LLM inference, where multi-core performance and memory bandwidth constraints may limit throughput.
